body.statement: For \(V=\{1,2,3,4\}\) with binary \(\{-1,+1\}\) states, the tuple \(\mathfrak u_{\star}\) is accepted by \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\). The table \(p_{\star}\) has exactly the elementary CIs \(1\perp2\), \(1\perp2\mid\{3,4\}\), \(3\perp4\), and \(3\perp4\mid\{1,2\}\). Among all \(543\) labelled DAGs, exactly \(50\) are I-maps, and the unique four-edge minima are \(D_A\) and \(D_B\), which lie in distinct MECs. Their probabilities for \(Y_3=+1\) under \(do(Y_1=+1)\) are \(13/20\) and \(1/2\), respectively.
body.justification: The finite instance proves that the target family is nonvacuous beyond one Markov equivalence class.
body.gap: The examples in Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo motivate tied sparsest outputs but do not provide this binary rational exact-oracle enumeration certificate.
body.consumer: Implementers obtain a unit test whose graph counts, oracle bits, and intervention gap are all checkable by exact arithmetic.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(t=t_\star=1/3\).  Summing the unnormalised numerator of \(p_\star\) over \(s_3\) and \(s_4\) gives
\[
 \sum_{s_3=\pm1}(1+ts_1s_3)(1+ts_2s_3)
   =2(1+t^2s_1s_2),
\]
\[
 \sum_{s_4=\pm1}(1+ts_1s_4)(1-ts_2s_4)
   =2(1-t^2s_1s_2). \tag{27}
\]
Their product is \(4(1-t^4)\), independently of \((s_1,s_2)\).  Summing over the four choices of \((s_1,s_2)\) yields \(16(1-t^4)\), exactly the denominator in the definition of \(p_\star\).  Thus the table is normalized.  Every numerator factor belongs to \(\{2/3,4/3\}\), so every cell is strictly positive.  In lexicographic \((-1,+1)\) order its cells are
\[
 \frac1{40}(4,4,1,1,4,1,4,1,1,4,1,4,1,1,4,4). \tag{28}
\]
In particular the table is rational and its minimum cell is \(1/40\).

Equation (27) gives \(p_\star(s_1,s_2)=1/4\), so \(1\perp2\).  Interchanging the pairs \((s_1,s_2)\) and \((s_3,s_4)\) gives \(p_\star(s_3,s_4)=1/4\), so \(3\perp4\).  Conditional on \((s_1,s_2)\), the numerator is a product of one function of \(s_3\) and one function of \(s_4\), proving \(3\perp4\mid\{1,2\}\).  Conditional on \((s_3,s_4)\), it is a product of one function of \(s_1\) and one function of \(s_2\), proving \(1\perp2\mid\{3,4\}\).

To show that there are no further elementary independences, for distinct \(i,j\) and \(C\subseteq V\setminus\{i,j\}\), use the binary conditional-independence minor
\[
 \Delta_{ij\mid C}(a,b,c)
 =p(a,b,c)p(c)-p(a,c)p(b,c). \tag{29}
\]
Direct integer summation from (28) gives the following nonzero minor for each of the other twenty statements.  In every row take \(a=b=-1\), and set all displayed coordinates of \(c\) equal to \(-1\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c@{\qquad}c|c|c}
(i,j)&C&\Delta&(i,j)&C&\Delta\\ \hline
(1,2)&\{3\}&-9/1600 &(1,2)&\{4\}&9/1600\\
(1,3)&\varnothing&3/40 &(1,3)&\{2\}&3/160\\
(1,3)&\{4\}&3/160 &(1,3)&\{2,4\}&3/1600\\
(1,4)&\varnothing&3/40 &(1,4)&\{2\}&3/160\\
(1,4)&\{3\}&3/160 &(1,4)&\{2,3\}&3/400\\
(2,3)&\varnothing&3/40 &(2,3)&\{1\}&3/160\\
(2,3)&\{4\}&3/160 &(2,3)&\{1,4\}&3/400\\
(2,4)&\varnothing&-3/40 &(2,4)&\{1\}&-3/160\\
(2,4)&\{3\}&-3/160 &(2,4)&\{1,3\}&-3/400\\
(3,4)&\{1\}&-9/1600 &(3,4)&\{2\}&9/1600
\end{array} \tag{30}
\]
The four factorizations just proved make every minor for the four asserted statements vanish, whereas (30) gives a nonzero minor for every remaining elementary statement.  Hence the displayed four are exact.

We next verify the graph counts without a genericity premise.  Inclusion--exclusion on the nonempty set of sources gives the number \(a_q\) of labelled DAGs on \(q\) vertices:
\[
 a_q=\sum_{k=1}^q(-1)^{k+1}{q\choose k}
       2^{k(q-k)}a_{q-k},
 \qquad a_0=1. \tag{31}
\]
Successive substitution yields \((a_0,a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4)=(1,1,3,25,543)\).

The nonzero minors in (30) show that each cross pair
\[
 \{1,3\},\ \{1,4\},\ \{2,3\},\ \{2,4\} \tag{32}
\]
is dependent given every subset of the other two vertices.  If a pair in (32) were nonadjacent in an I-map DAG, take its later endpoint in a topological order.  The earlier endpoint is then a nonparent nondescendant, so the DAG local Markov property d-separates the pair given the later endpoint's parent set, a subset of the other two vertices.  This contradicts (30).  Thus all four edges in (32) occur in every I-map, and no I-map has fewer than four edges.

At four edges the skeleton is therefore the four-cycle formed by (32).  Of its \(16\) orientations, precisely the two directed cycles are not acyclic.  Checking the collider status on the two paths between each opposite pair in the remaining \(14\) orientations gives exactly two I-maps:
\[
 \{1\to3,1\to4,2\to3,2\to4\},
 \qquad
 \{3\to1,3\to2,4\to1,4\to2\}. \tag{33}
\]
The first implies only \(1\perp2\) and \(3\perp4\mid\{1,2\}\) among nonadjacent-pair statements; the second implies only \(3\perp4\) and \(1\perp2\mid\{3,4\}\).  Every other acyclic orientation makes one opposite pair d-separated under a conditioning set ruled out by (30).  These are exactly \(D_A\) and \(D_B\).

For completeness, the higher-edge counts can also be obtained directly.  A five-edge skeleton is \(K_4\) with one missing pair.  The missing pair must be \(\{1,2\}\) or \(\{3,4\}\), since all cross pairs are forced by (32).  For \(K_4\setminus\{a,b\}\), with remaining vertices \(c,d\), its \(18\) acyclic orientations have the following exhaustive active-path classification:
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrr}
\text{unique set }C\text{ with }a\mathbin{\perp_D}b\mid C
 &\varnothing&\{c\}&\{d\}&\{c,d\}\\ \hline
\text{number of orientations}&2&3&3&10.
\end{array} \tag{34}
\]
To verify (34), orient the four edges incident to \(a,b\), orient \(c-d\), discard an orientation exactly when one of the two resulting triangles is directed, and inspect the two length-two and two length-three paths from \(a\) to \(b\); these five binary arrow choices give the four displayed counts \(2,3,3,10\), summing to \(18\).  For the missing pair \(\{1,2\}\), precisely the \(2+10=12\) orientations associated with \(C=\varnothing\) or \(C=\{3,4\}\) are I-maps.  By symmetry another \(12\) arise when the missing pair is \(\{3,4\}\).  Finally, a complete four-node DAG entails no nontrivial d-separation and is automatically an I-map; there are \(4!=24\) such acyclic orientations.  Hence the exact number of I-maps is
\[
 2+12+12+24=50, \tag{35}
\]
and (33) are the unique four-edge minima.  They are in different Markov equivalence classes because \(D_A\) d-separates \(1\) and \(2\), while \(D_B\) does not, and \(D_B\) d-separates \(3\) and \(4\), while \(D_A\) does not.

The two required DAG factorizations follow from the four established conditional independences.  Under \(D_A\), truncation at \(s_1=+1\) and summation over \(s_2,s_4\) give
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_\star)
 =\sum_{s_2}p_\star(s_2)
   p_\star(s_3=+1\mid s_1=+1,s_2)
 =p_\star(s_3=+1\mid s_1=+1), \tag{36}
\]
where the last equality uses \(1\perp2\).  Direct sign summation in the displayed family gives uniform one-variable marginals and
\[
 \mathbb E_{p_t}(s_1s_3)
 =\frac{t(1-t^2)}{1-t^4}
 =\frac{t}{1+t^2}. \tag{37}
\]
With \(t=1/3\), (36)--(37) imply
\[
 T_{D_A,+1}(p_\star)
 =\frac12+\frac{t}{2(1+t^2)}
 =\frac{13}{20}. \tag{38}
\]
Under \(D_B\), node \(3\) is an unmanipulated root.  Removing the factor for intervened node \(1\) and summing the other normalized kernels gives
\[
 T_{D_B,+1}(p_\star)=p_\star(s_3=+1)=\frac12. \tag{39}
\]
The factorizations just used make \(p_\star\) Markov to the respective DAGs, and strict positivity was proved from (28).  Therefore \(\mathrm{lem{:}dag\text{-}intervention\text{-}functional}\) identifies (38)--(39) with the probabilities of \(Y_3=+1\) under \(do(Y_1=+1)\), rather than merely with regression functionals.  The finite supports, disjoint query sets, empty background set, exact oracle from (29)--(30), exhaustive family from (31)--(35), and verified rational table satisfy every check in \(\mathrm{def{:}certified\text{-}input}\).  Thus \(\mathfrak u_\star\) is accepted and all claims follow.
